issues.legal_issue: Court fee in a suit seeking cancellation of a document creating rights in property is computed on the value of the property for which the document was executed, rather than its current market value.
material_facts: The plaintiff sued to cancel a power of attorney after alleging that it had been misused to transfer her property to the attorney’s husband.
The plaintiff amended the suit to seek cancellation of the sale deed transferring the property and paid court fee by reference to the value stated for the property in that deed.
The lower courts directed the plaintiff to pay court fee based on the property’s market value.
issues.conclusion: The court set aside the orders requiring court fee on market value. For cancellation of the sale deed, the fee is to be computed on the value of the property for which the deed was executed, not its market value.
issues.legal_principle: Section 40(1) of the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959, supplies a special rule for cancellation suits: the value is the amount or property value for which the document was executed, and the wording does not make market value the basis. Section 7(1), which begins ‘Save as otherwise provided’, does not displace that specific rule. The court applied the plain-meaning approach in Kanai Lal Sur v. Paramnidhi Sadhukhan and the rule against adding or rewriting statutory words in Union of India v. Deoki Nandan Aggarwal and Shyam Kishori Devi v. Patna Municipal Corporation. It approved Venkata Narasimha Raju v. Chandrayya, Navaraja v. Kaliappa Gounder, Arunachalathammal v. Sudalaimuthu Pillai, Andalammal v. B. Kanniah, and Allam Venkateswara Reddy v. Golla Venkatanarayana. It distinguished the Full Bench decision in Kutumba Sastri v. Sundaramma because that case interpreted differently worded legislation, and held that contrary Kerala High Court decisions did not state the correct law.

rule.if: cancellation_suit and document_creates_property_rights and whole_document_challenged and document_states_property_value

predicates.cancellation_suit: A plaintiff brings a suit seeking cancellation of a document.
predicates.document_creates_property_rights: The document purports or operates to create, declare, assign, limit, or extinguish rights in property.
predicates.whole_document_challenged: The plaintiff seeks cancellation of the entire document rather than only a part of it.
predicates.document_states_property_value: The document states the value of the property for which it was executed.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks cancellation of an entire property-rights document that states the property’s value, the court fee is computed on the value for which the document was executed.
